chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever shaves his head or plucks the hair of his armpit, forgetting or heedless or ignorant, there is no penalty upon him. And whoever does it deliberately, then upon him is the blood (damm).'

key_terms.دَمٌ: blood (a specific ritual penalty or fine)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for deliberately shaving one's head or plucking armpit hair in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Isfabar, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the ruling on shaving the head or plucking armpit hair, distinguishing between unintentional acts (forgetfulness, heedlessness, or ignorance) which incur no penalty, and deliberate acts which require the payment of 'damm' (blood). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that minor ritual impurities or physical changes do not necessarily invalidate worship unless performed with intent, emphasizing the mercy and flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding daily grooming practices.
